Present Perfect Continuous vs. Present Perfect
Both the Present Perfect and the Present Perfect Continuous are used to express that an action began in the past and is still going on or has just finished.

We use the Present Perfect
  • to talk about something that started in the past and continues to the present
  • to talk about something we have done several times in the past and continue to do
  • when we talk about our experience up to the present
  • to talk about something that happened in the past but is important at the time of speaking

We use the Present Perfect Continuous
  • to describe something changing or developing up to now
Sometimes there's no difference in meaning between the two tenses. This is especially true with the verbs live, work and study.

You put a relative clause immediately after the noun it talks about.
You use a relative clause with which for things to make the thing you are talking about clearer.
In spoken English and written English that often replaces which or who. Which is generally more formal than that.

Research into how robots function and their potential uses has grown substantially since the early 20th century. In 1939, Westinghouse built ‘Elektro', who was humanoid in appearance, for the World's Fair. The robot, which relied on motors, photoelectric cells, relays and record players, performed 26 routines.

Since then, robotic engineers have been crafting robots to look, feel and act more human. They have been hoping this will make it easier for us to warm to machines that we see as cold.

They have been working toward creating robots that sense your touch and turn to greet you. They have noted that subtle actions help bring robots to life. Artificial eyes that move and blink, slight chest movements that simulate breathing, and man-made muscles to change facial expressions, are all attributes socially acceptable robots of the future must have.

Scientists have also been working on robotic pets. With no feeding required, a robotic dinosaur that recognizes sounds, sights, and touch, craves affection, and explores its environment is an alternative that any child would take to. Wouldn't you?
